title: Injectivity of the canonical raw affine cohomology colimit comparison
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $I$ a nonempty directed preorder, and $D:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Over}(S)$ a system with affine transitions and qcqs structure maps. Let $c$ be a cone whose underlying scheme cone is limiting and whose structure map is qcqs. Write $g_i:X_i\to S$, $g:X\to S$, and $f_i:X\to X_i$ for the structure maps and cone projections. Let $F_i$ be abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] with unital coherent inverse-image transitions $\varphi_{ji}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], with the identity and composition HEq equations displayed in the Lean signature. Let $H:I\to\mathrm{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathrm{Ab})$, $eH_i:H_i\simeq f_i^{-1}F_i$, and the canonical transition equation $hH$ present the pulled-back coefficient system; set $F=\operatorname{colim}H$. Fix $p\in\mathbf N$ and an affine etale object $U$ of $S$. Define $P_i(U)=\operatorname{Hom}((g_i^{-1}\mathbf Z[U])[0],F_i[0][p])$ and $P(U)=\operatorname{Hom}((g^{-1}\mathbf Z[U])[0],F[0][p])$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with the explicit raw pullback functions of [lem-sbc-abelian-higher-direct-image-natural-comparison]. There exist a functor $K:I\to\mathrm{Ab}$, a cocone $B$ on $K$, additive isomorphisms $e_i:P_i(U)\simeq K_i$ and $e:P(U)\simeq B_{\mathrm{pt}}$, such that for every arrow $a:i\to j$ and raw class $t\in P_i(U)$ one has $K(a)(e_i(t))=e_j(\operatorname{rawPullback}_{a,\varphi_a}(t))$, and $B_i(e_i(t))=e(\operatorname{rawPullback}_{f_i,(eH_i)^{-1};\iota_i}(t))$. Furthermore the canonical group homomorphism $\operatorname{colim}K\to B_{\mathrm{pt}}$, namely colimit.desc K B, is injective. No eventual-zero statement, restriction family, or surjectivity is part of this assertion. The raw stage functions and the raw maps to the limit are supplied by additive natural transformations tau_a:P_i to P_j and beta_i:P_i to P, on the entire small etale site of S. Their components at every etale V are required to equal the explicit raw pullback functions just specified. The transition and leg equations on the fixed affine U are expressed using these components. This is naturality of the canonical maps, with no eventual-zero or uniform-vanishing conclusion.

proof.text: Form the pullback diagram with stage U times_S X_i and limit U times_S X, taking maps from pullback universal properties. The same universal property proves the limit assertion. Qcqs morphisms remain qcqs after base change; since U is affine the stages are qcqs schemes. Affine transition morphisms remain affine. Restrict the sheaves and their transition maps along the second projections, transport the identity, composition and H-transition laws through the inverse-image composition isomorphisms, and put all sheaves into degree-zero single complexes, zero below zero. Inverse image, being a left adjoint, preserves the coefficient colimit; termwise colimits of single complexes are again single complexes. This supplies D,c,hc,compact,quasiSeparated,affine,F,phi,hidentity,hcomposition,a,hbelow,G,eG,hG,L,hL in the presentation.

proof.text: Take H to be the stage cohomology groups of these single complexes. Define their maps by the canonical derived pullback followed by the transition complex map. Define P by homology applied to the derived adjunction unit and the composition comparison with global sections: this is exactly hP in the presentation. Pullback and coefficient composition give hH. At the limit take B with these canonical cohomology groups and their pullback/coefficient legs; this gives eH,eB and hB, with no assertion that B is a colimit. Before evaluating on U, construct the raw maps as additive natural transformations tau and beta on the small etale site. Additivity follows because the derived pullback functor is additive and precomposition/postcomposition in a preadditive category are additive. For restriction V to W, naturality of the inverse-image composition comparison and the single-functor comparison moves the source precomposition across these two factors; derived pullback preserves composition. Postcompose with the same shift and coefficient maps. This proves the naturality square; the components are the explicit raw functions by construction. Evaluate tau and beta on U to obtain exactly the prescribed diagram transitions and cocone legs.

source.place: Lemma 59.51.7 proof, base change to affine etale U; Tag 03Q8 restricted-cohomology presentation, and Tag 0EZM canonical maps of complexes

proof.text: The sheafification/free-forgetful/Yoneda adjunctions identify maps from the free abelian represented sheaf with sections on the corresponding etale object. Its inverse image represents sections on U times_S X_i. Restriction to this etale scheme preserves injectives because its left adjoint is exact: extension by zero is the sheafification of the direct sum over lifts, and exactness can be checked on geometric stalks, where it is a direct sum of abelian groups. Apply this sections equivalence to a bounded-below injective resolution and identify derived Hom from the degree-zero free sheaf with restricted cohomology. The fully faithful bounded-below inclusion identifies the resulting Hom groups with unbounded derived cohomology of the single complexes. This supplies additive stageIso and limitIso. Naturality of these adjunctions and of the inverse-image single/shift comparisons identifies each cocone leg with exactly raw pullback and the specified coefficient map, proving compatibility. This construction uses no class descent or continuity conclusion. The same naturality calculation for each stage transition yields K.map a (e_i.hom t) = e_j.hom (rawPullback_a t), not just the coprojection compatibility. Thus the isomorphisms identify both diagrams and cocones with the specified raw functions. The empty affine object has zero groups, and degree zero is the ordinary sections adjunction. In particular all restrictions commute with the components of tau and beta, since these have been constructed as natural transformations; this assertion is before cohomology continuity and asserts no stage vanishing.

source.place: Restricted cohomology presentation; the proof refers to Cohomology on Sites 21.7.4 and 21.20.3; explicit derived-Hom naturality elaboration by N2

proof.text: Apply the existing complex cohomology continuity theorem to the base-changed qcqs scheme system and the single coefficient complexes of common lower bound zero constructed in the preceding steps. Its conclusion says that the canonical cohomology cocone B is colimiting. Hence colimit.desc K B is an isomorphism. In the category of abelian groups every isomorphism is injective, giving the asserted comparison injectivity. Only this half of continuity is retained. Package these canonical maps and their equations in RawAffineColimitComparisonData, whose fields are actual categorical data and proofs; its Nonempty assertion uses no choice to define an object.
